name: CULTURE SENSITIVITY-STOOL
description: Stool Culture & Sensitivity identifies enteric pathogens causing gastroenteritis and determines antibiotic susceptibility. This test diagnoses bacterial diarrhea and guides targeted therapy.

testdeatils.method: Conventional Culture with Antibiotic Susceptibility Testing
testdeatils.instrumentation: Automated Culture Systems (BD BACTEC, bioMérieux VITEK)

literatureReview: Stool Culture & Sensitivity diagnoses bacterial gastroenteritis. Common pathogens include Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, Yersinia, and pathogenic E. coli. Sample collected in sterile container, transported immediately or in Cary-Blair transport medium. Inoculated onto selective and differential media (MacConkey, XLD, Campylobacter agar). Incubated at appropriate temperatures. Antibiotic susceptibility testing performed on isolated pathogens. Most diarrhea is viral or self-limiting; culture indicated for severe cases, bloody diarrhea, or immunocompromised patients. TAT 24-72 hours. Results guide antibiotic therapy for invasive infections. Negative culture doesn't rule out infection if sample collection poor or pathogen fastidious.
